title: Stomping off tunes and waltzes; today's teenage crowds
summary: Leaders counted off tunes; waltzes were played plenty in the halls, while teenagers now want rock and roll and small combos with a singer.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: When they, when you, when you start a key, did the leader stump off for you? Yeah, he stumped.
How'd he stump off? He's done.
And he gone, see. Two, two. Two. Sometimes it's three. You know what that mean? One, two, three. Waltz. A little fast.
Yeah. Did you play many waltzes in the old days? Oh yeah.

Played plenty waltzes. Yeah, played plenty waltzes. That's all they mostly used to play, pretty waltzes. And especially these halls down there. Well, in the coppery's in the economy hall, that used to take too. You had to play waltzes. But on the late watch, when it's getting late, around 12 o'clock, play waltzes. They want to clap it back. That time they play waltzes over three, four times. Because some of the people, they want some nice waltzes sometime. But now they don't care. You can play waltzes now. They talk about you. You can play waltzes. Of course, you go up to country and some of them plays where the older people is, where they have dancers, they love to play to hear the whole same old band, the same old waltzes, you see. Some people don't want you to do, but the teenagers just sitting down and going to sleep. Well, that makes you don't have no show with the teenagers. But you're just good with the old, the older people. But you got to get in with the teenagers now. Them the ones that gives the partisan thing. If you don't play for them, nah, they don't. They sit up and look at you. That's all. They ain't no dang. Now we played a place over in Urode that had a good band. It was a Dixieland on rap. But we played there. I don't think I'm going to go back there in the movie. They wasn't charging but the dialing cord to come in and they said the music was all right swell, but that ain't our type of music. You see? That's what they do. Well, we know we was praying, but they was praying what they knew. They couldn't pray nothing else. But I had to pick up some kind of stuff on there, you see. Make it sound good. And then get us to sing. They had a singer and I just played with the singer. But they didn't have to play much. And me and the singer and the drum, bass, that's all they wanted. They read it that in the whole band. Yeah, yeah. That's why they hardly use a trumpet today. You take that piano and the guitar and the bass or a bass drum and a saxophone and you don't need nothing else if you got a singer. You can make it anywhere with that. They ain't looking for no big pile of music.
